accepted.question_text: For bounded convex domains in C^N, are the visibility notion introduced in [15] and the weaker visibility notion introduced by Bharali and Zimmer actually equivalent in full generality? The paper states that, in bounded convex domains, the notion used in [15] is equivalent to a weaker form of Bharali and Zimmer's definition, but leaves open whether the two definitions coincide without further assumptions.

evidence.quote: [19], the visibility notion introduced in [15] is equivalent to a weaker form of the notion introduced by Bharali and Zimmer. It remains an open question whether, in general, those two definitions are equivalent.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a bounded convex domain Ω ⊂ C^N whose boundary contains no non-trivial analytic discs, such that Ω is essentially visible but not visible? Here, essential visibility means that for each pair of distinct boundary points p and q there is a compact set K ⊂⊂ Ω such that, whenever interior points z_k → p and w_k → q are chosen, one can find geodesic segments joining z_k to w_k that meet K; visibility is the stronger requirement that every such sequence of geodesic segments must eventually meet a fixed compact set.

evidence.quote: Question 3.3. Does there exist a bounded convex domain Ω ⊂ C^N with no non-trivial analytic discs in the boundary which is essentially visible but not visible?

We say that p and q are essentially visible if there exists a compact set K ⊂⊂ Ω such that for every sequences {zk}, {wk} ⊂ Ω so that {zk} converges to p and {wk} converges to q there exists a sequence of geodesic segments {γk} such that γk(0) = zk, γk(1) = wk and γk(sk) ∈ K for some sk ∈ (0, 1) and for all k.

We say that p and q are strongly visible if there exists a compact set K ⊂⊂ Ω so that for every sequence of geodesic segments {γk} such that {γk(0)} converges to p and {γk(1)} converges to q there is sk ∈ (0, 1) such that γk(sk) ∈ K for all k sufficiently large.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a smoothly bounded convex domain Ω ⊂ C^N that is essentially visible but not visible? Equivalently, can smooth convex boundary regularity still allow the gap between essential visibility and the stronger visibility property defined via geodesic segments meeting a fixed compact set?

evidence.quote: Does there exist a smoothly bounded convex domain Ω ⊂ C^N which is essentially visible but not visible?
If every p, q ∈ ∂Ω, p ̸= q are essentially visible, we say that Ω is essentially visible. While, if every p, q ∈ ∂Ω, p ̸= q are strongly visible, we say that Ω is visible.

accepted.question_text: Let Ω ⊂ C^N be a bounded convex domain, and let {γ_k} be a sequence of non-visible geodesic segments, meaning that the images γ_k([0,1]) eventually avoid every compact subset of Ω while the endpoints satisfy γ_k(0) → p and γ_k(1) → q for distinct boundary points p,q ∈ ∂Ω. If Γ({γ_k}) denotes the set of boundary cluster points of interior points γ_{k_n}(t_{k_n}) with t_{k_n} ∈ [0,1], must any two distinct points p,q ∈ Γ({γ_k}) satisfy one of the following alternatives: either the open real segment {tp + (1 − t)q : 0 < t < 1} lies in Ω, or the closed real segment {tp + (1 − t)q : 0 ≤ t ≤ 1} lies in ∂Ω and the complex affine line C(p − q) + q does not intersect Ω?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.5. Let Ω ⊂ C^N be a bounded convex domain. Let {γk} be a sequence of non-visible geodesic segments and let Γ({γk}) := {p ∈ ∂Ω : ∃{tkn } ⊂ [0, 1] : limn→∞ γkn(tkn) = p}. If p, q ∈ Γ({γk}) and p ̸= q then • either {tp + (1 − t)q, 0 < t < 1} ⊂ Ω, • or, {tp + (1 − t)q, 0 ≤ t ≤ 1} ⊂ ∂Ω and (C(p − q) + q) ∩ Ω = ∅.

We say that {γk} is a sequence of non-visible geodesic segments if (1) for every compact set K ⊂⊂ Ω there exists k0 such that γk([0, 1]) ∩ K = ∅ for all k ≥ k0, (2) there exist p, q ∈ ∂Ω, p ̸= q such that limk→∞ γk(0) = p and limk→∞ γk(1) = q.

accepted.question_text: Let Ω ⊂ C^N be a bounded convex domain and let F0 be the family of complex geodesics φ : D → Ω parametrized so that δ_Ω(φ(0)) = max_{ζ∈D} δ_Ω(φ(ζ)), where δ_Ω(z) is the Euclidean distance from z to ∂Ω. Nikolov's theorem states that Ω is visible if and only if (1) ∂Ω contains no non-trivial analytic discs and (2) F0 is uniformly equicontinuous. Is condition (2) alone already sufficient to imply visibility, even without separately assuming the absence of non-trivial analytic discs in the boundary?

evidence.quote: Theorem 3.6 (Nikolov). Let Ω ⊂ C^N be a bounded convex domain. Then Ω is visible if and only if (1) ∂Ω does not contain non-trivial analytic discs, (2) F0 is uniformly equicontinuous
Is it not clear whether condition (2) in the previous theorem implies visibility by itself, but presumably it does.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a non-visible bounded convex domain Ω such that every complex geodesic φ : D → Ω extends continuously to the closed unit disc up to the boundary ∂D? Equivalently, is the property that all complex geodesics extend continuously to the boundary sufficient to force visibility of a bounded convex domain?

evidence.quote: Question 3.7. Does there exist a non-visible bounded convex domain Ω such that every complex geodesic φ : D → Ω extends continuously up to ∂D? In other words, is the continuous extension of all complex geodesics up to the boundary sufficient for visibility?

accepted.question_text: For a bounded convex domain Ω ⊂ C^N, is visibility equivalent to complex visibility? Here, complex visibility means that for every pair of distinct boundary points p and q there exists a compact set K ⊂⊂ Ω such that, whenever interior sequences z_k → p and w_k → q are given, every sequence of complex geodesics φ_k with z_k,w_k ∈ φ_k(D) must satisfy φ_k(D) ∩ K ≠ ∅ for all sufficiently large k.

evidence.quote: Definition 3.8. Let Ω ⊂ C^N be a bounded convex domain. We say that Ω is complex visible if for every p, q ∈ ∂Ω such that p ̸= q there exist a compact set K ⊂⊂ Ω such that for every sequences {zk}, {wk} ⊂ Ω so that {zk} converges to p and {wk} converges to q every sequence of complex geodesics {φk} such that zk, wk ∈ φk(D) has the property that φk(D) ∩ K ̸= ∅ for large enough k.
Conjecture 3.9. Let Ω ⊂ C^N be a bounded convex domain. Then Ω is visible if and only if it is complex visible.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a bounded convex domain Ω that is not visible but for which every geodesic ray lands, meaning that for every geodesic ray γ : [0,+∞) → Ω the limit lim_{t→∞} γ(t) exists in the Euclidean boundary?

evidence.quote: In particular, all geodesic rays land (that is, if γ : [0, +∞) → Ω is a geodesic ray in Ω, then limt→∞ γ(t) exists).
Question 3.10. Does there exist a bounded convex domain Ω which is not visible and such that all geodesic rays land?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω ⊂ C^N be a bounded convex domain and fix z0 ∈ Ω. Let G_{z0} be the family of all geodesic segments and geodesic rays starting at z0, parametrized by hyperbolic arc length. Is Ω visible if and only if G_{z0} is uniformly equicontinuous as a family of maps from [0,+∞) with the Euclidean topology into C^N with the Euclidean topology?
accepted.context_brief: equicontinuity of geodesic segments and rays

evidence.quote: Let z0 ∈ Ω and let Gz0 be the family of all geodesic segments and geodesic rays starting from z0, parameterized in hyperbolic arc-length.

Conjecture 3.11. Let Ω ⊂ C^N be a bounded convex domain. Then Ω is visible if and only if Gz0 is uniformly equicontinuous (as family of functions from [0, +∞) endowed with the Euclidean topology to C^N endowed with the Euclidean topology).

accepted.question_text: Let Ω ⊂ C^N be a bounded convex domain whose boundary contains no non-trivial analytic discs. Does Ω have the Denjoy-Wolff property if and only if, for every sequential horosphere E_{z0}({z_n},R) determined by a sequence z_n → p ∈ ∂Ω and radius R>0, the closure of that horosphere meets the boundary ∂Ω at exactly one point?

evidence.quote: The previous proposition implies that if the closure of any sequential horosphere of a bounded convex domain without non-trivial analytic discs on its boundary touches the boundary at exactly one point, then the domain possesses the Denjoy-Wolff property.

Conjecture 4.8. Let Ω ⊂ C^N be a bounded convex domain. Assume ∂Ω does not contain non-trivial analytic discs. Then Ω has the Denjoy-Wolff property if and only if the closure of any sequential horosphere touches ∂Ω at just one point.

accepted.question_text: For a bounded convex domain Ω ⊂ C^N, is visibility equivalent to the Denjoy-Wolff property? In other words, does Ω enjoy the Denjoy-Wolff property exactly when every pair of distinct boundary points is visible in the sense studied in the paper?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.9. Let Ω ⊂ C^N be a bounded convex domain. Then Ω is visible if and only if it enjoys the Denjoy-Wolff property.

accepted.question_text: Let N ≥ 1 and let F : D^N → D^N be a holomorphic self-map of the polydisc with no fixed points. Must there exist an index j ∈ {1,…,N} and a boundary point σ ∈ ∂D such that, for every starting point z ∈ D^N, the j-th coordinate of the iterates converges to σ, that is, lim_{n→∞} π_j(F^n(z)) = σ?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.1. Let N ≥ 1 and let F : D^N → D^N be holomorphic and without fixed points. Then there exist j ∈ {1, . . . , N} and σ ∈ ∂D such that limn→∞ πj(F◦n(z)) = σ for all z ∈ D^N, where πj(z) = zj (the projection on the j-th component).

accepted.question_text: Suppose Ω = D_1 × ··· × D_ℓ, where each D_j is a bounded convex domain in C^{N_j}, the dimensions satisfy N_1 + ··· + N_ℓ = N ≥ 2, and each factor D_j has the Denjoy-Wolff property. If F : Ω → Ω is holomorphic and has no fixed points in Ω, must there exist an index j_0 ∈ {1,…,ℓ} and a boundary point p_{j_0} ∈ ∂D_{j_0} such that the j_0-th coordinate projection π_{j_0}(F^m(z)) converges to p_{j_0} for every z ∈ Ω as m → ∞?

evidence.quote: Question 5.5. Assume that Ω = D1 × . . . × Dℓ, where Dj is a bounded convex domain in C^{Nj}, j = 1, . . . , ℓ and N1 + . . . + Nℓ = N ≥ 2. Suppose Dj has the Denjoy-Wolff property for every j = 1, . . . , ℓ. Let F : Ω → Ω be holomorphic and such that F has no fixed points in Ω. Is it true that there exist j0 ∈ {1, . . . , ℓ} and pj0 ∈ ∂Dj0 such that {πj0(F◦m(z))} converges to pj0 for all z ∈ Ω as m → ∞?
